title: Statistical Rethinking Seminars
text:
1 Preface
These pages include notes and resources for the Statistical Rethinking Seminars at the Faculty of Social and Health Sciences, at the University of Inland Norway. The seminar series is organized as a course accredited as part of the PhD program Health and Welfare.

title: Statistical Rethinking Seminars
text:
1.1 What and How we learn
This series of seminars is based on the book Statistical Rethinking by Richard McElreath. The book introduces Bayesian statistics and probabilistic programming in the context of scientific research. The book helps you to develop a principled approach to statistical analysis.
We will meet every week for discussions. Meetings will be held as seminars to discuss the book’s material and exercises. This learning strategy requires you to prepare to participate actively in discussions. Preparation includes reading the relevant chapters, watching the lectures, and working on the exercises. Many exercises require coding in your preferred coding environment. The book mostly includes R code, but other programming languages have also been used to work on the material (see resources).
The seminar series follows the same structure as the course given by Richard McElreath (in 2025) Table 1.1. Beginning on the 22nd of January 2026, we will meet weekly for 10 weeks.

title: Statistical Rethinking Seminars
text:
1.2 Prerequisites and resources
There are no formal prerequisites for the seminar series. However, knowing basic R programming will make your experience easier when reading the book, watching the lectures, and completing the exercises. Experience with statistical analysis will also be helpful. The final assignment in the course will require you to perform a data analysis on data of your choosing. It is expected that the analysis is performed using reproducible programming. The R programming language and auxiliary tools are discussed here, along with instructions for setting up software for reproducible programming.
You can find resources related to Bayesian modelling here

title: 2  Resources
text:
2.0.1 Introductions to Bayesian inference

Rasmus Bååth has created a three-part video-lecture introducing Bayesian data analysis Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3.
A visual introduction to Bayesian inference



2.0.2 Resources for fitting and learning Bayesian data modelling

Statistical rethinking with brms, ggplot2, and the tidyverse: Second edition by Solomon Kurz is a thorough parallel reading of Statistical Rethinking with all models implemented in the brms package.
The brms Book: Applied Bayesian Regression Modelling Using R and Stan (Early Draft) by Paul Bürkner. This book introduces the brms package along with Bayesian regression modelling.
The stan user guide by the Stan Development Team provides examples on programming models in the Stan language.

title: 3  Writing mathematical notation in quarto files
text:
3.1 Why use mathematical notation?
A quarto document can contain output from code chunks based on data, code and other technical content, including mathematical notation. \(\LaTeX\) syntax is a well described system for writing mathematical notation, for example, in quarto files.
Similar to other written languages, mathematical notation helps you develop and communicate ideas. In this course we will use formal descriptions of models to describe assumptions and what the code does.

text:
3.2 Using \(\LaTeX\) syntax in quarto documents
We can add inline mathematics using $1 + 2 = 3$, this will render to \(1+2=3\). Using two $ signs will put the equation on a new line.
$$ 1 + 2 = 3$$
